scenario.name: VMware/Broadcom, CISA AA23-039A & Mandiant DFIR — ESXi /var/log/shell.log, hostd.log & VMDK Hypervisor Forensics
scenario.overview: Think of a bright neighborhood supermarket filled with stocked grocery aisles, rolling shopping carts, barcode price stickers, and busy checkout conveyor belts. Pushing a metal shopping cart down the supermarket aisles, a shopper peels a cheap barcode sticker off a small item and presses it cleanly onto a high-value boxed product. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the barcode price scanner in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the barcode price scanner in tiny disguised batches. When the store manager reconciles the checkout receipt tape against the aisle inventory count and overhead camera, the swapped barcode trick is caught red-handed. In this scenario (T1078, VMware/Broadcom, CISA AA23-039A & Mandiant DFIR, ESXi /var/log/shell.log, hostd.log & VMDK Hypervisor Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: eSXi SSH Authentication, then mass Virtual Machine Termination via esxcli, then intermittent VMDK Encryption. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ESXi SSH Authentication, then Mass Virtual Machine Termination via esxcli, then Intermittent VMDK Encryption, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1078 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 2: Mass Virtual Machine Termination via esxcli vm process kill (/var/log/hostd.log)
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1529 - System Shutdown/Reboot: Hypervisor VM Termination)
stages.description: At the checkout lane, the cashier slides the box across the glowing barcode scanner, which blindly trusts the swapped sticker instead of inspecting what is inside the box. Here in Step 2 inside the supermarket, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the barcode price scanner in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the locked stockroom back door. Because running vmx hypervisor processes hold exclusive file locks on guest virtual disks (-flat.vmdk), the actor iterates through every World ID and runs esxcli vm process kill --type=force --world-id=<ID>.
